title: Los Angeles weather: Southern California to see warmer temperatures as Santa Ana winds linger, rain possible by next week - ABC7 Los Angeles
text:
Los Angeles weather: Southern California to see warmer temperatures as Santa Ana winds linger, rain possible by next week - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Weather 
 SoCal to see warmer temperatures as Santa Ana winds linger 
 Sunday, November 8, 2026 2:50PM 
 Este artículo se ofrece en Español Southern California will see hotter temperatures Sunday as Santa Ana winds linger. LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- Southern California will see hotter temperatures on Sunday as Santa Ana winds linger.
 The National Weather Service issued coastal alerts as high tides are expected.
 A beach hazard statement will be in effect through Tuesday morning along the coast of Ventura and L.A. counties. High tides of 7.2 to 7.6 feet are expected each morning. Expect 3 to 6 feet of surf.
 The Orange County coast will be under a coastal flood advisory through noon Tuesday. The National Weather Service said high tide is expected to peak at 7.4 to 7.6 feet Sunday and Monday. Surf will also increase.
 ABC7 has issued a Weather Change Alert for next Friday, as the possibility of rain enters the forecast.
 Sunday forecast
 Los Angeles and Orange counties can expect a high of 85 degrees with a low of 59 on Sunday. Expect similar conditions all week before rain chances and cooler temperatures move in next weekend.
 The valleys and the Inland Empire will see a high of 86 degrees and a low of 59 on Sunday. Similar conditions are on tap all week until rain chances begin on Friday.
 Beach communities can expect sunny conditions on Sunday, with a high of 84 degrees and a low of 67.
 Mountain areas will see sunny skies on Sunday, with a high of 64 degrees and a low of 31. Expect sunshine and highs in the low-60s all week.
 Deserts are expected to reach a high of 76 degrees and a low of 38 on Sunday. Palm Springs is expected to reach a high of 86 degrees.
